mainTopic: טובת הנאה: whether the owner's right to choose who gets מעשר עני and priestly gifts counts as a benefit or as money, applied to vows against benefit.
overview: The גמרא asks whether a woman who vowed not to benefit from people may take מעשר עני. The answer depends on טובת הנאה, the owner's right to choose which poor person gets the tithe. רב יוסף tries to tie this to the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and חכמים about the מעשר עני of דמאי. אביי rejects that proof. He says the argument is really about whether עמי הארץ are suspected of skipping מעשר עני. רבא settles the sources a different way. Tithe handed out at home, where the Torah says 'give,' carries טובת הנאה, so she may not take it. Tithe left at the threshing floor, where the Torah says 'leave,' carries none, so she may take it. Next the גמרא finds a contradiction in our משנה about whether טובת הנאה is worth money. רב הושעיא answers that the two halves follow רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who argue about how much a thief pays for stolen טבל. The explanation of that argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The view of חכמים on the poor man's tithe of דמאי
steps.stepSummary: The source being quoted ends with the view of חכמים: for דמאי, a person must name the מעשר עני, but he does not have to actually separate it and give it away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: he must designate the poor man's tithe by name, but he does not need to actually set it aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote of a source about the מעשר עני of דמאי. רב יוסף is about to use this source in his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that you do not even need to name the מעשר עני of דמאי. חכמים say you must name it, which shows the produce is treated as forbidden until you do. You still keep the tithe yourself, because a poor person cannot claim it without proof that it was never separated.

keyTerms.meaning: Designates by name, meaning he says 'this portion is the tithe.'
To actually set aside and give away.
Produce bought from an עם הארץ, who may not have tithed it.
Poor man's tithe, given in the 3rd and 6th years of the שמיטה cycle.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
He designates it by name, but he does not need to set it aside.
phrases.notes: This is talking about the מעשר עני of produce bought from an עם הארץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: קוֹרֵא שֵׁם, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְהַפְרִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a source quote that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For דמאי, the מעשר עני must be named but does not have to be given away.

steps.title: רב יוסף explains the view of חכמים: the owner has טובת הנאה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף suggests that חכמים hold a doubt makes the produce טבל, and that this goes together with the owner having טובת הנאה. If so, a woman who vowed off benefit from people cannot take מעשר עני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it true that the one who says the doubt makes it טבל holds that the owner has the benefit of choosing who gets it? And since he has that benefit, taking מעשר עני does not help her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף starts building a proof from the source. He explains the view of חכמים in a way that connects to טובת הנאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים require naming the tithe, so they must hold that a doubt about tithing makes the produce טבל. רב יוסף links this to the owner having טובת הנאה. If the owner chooses who gets the tithe, the woman who vowed would be getting a benefit from him, so she may not take it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Isn't it that...?' This opens a suggested proof.
A doubt about whether it was tithed makes it forbidden as טבל.
The owner's right to choose which poor person receives the gift.
It doesn't work.

phrases.english: What, is it not
that according to the one who says its doubt makes it טבל
he holds: the owner has the benefit of discretion,
and since he has the benefit of discretion
it does not work.
phrases.notes: He means that taking מעשר עני doesn't help the woman who vowed not to benefit from people.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו, לְמַאן דְּאָמַר סְפֵקוֹ טוֹבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the quoted source as proof for the טובת הנאה question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the owner of מעשר עני has טובת הנאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and חכמים about the מעשר עני of דמאי.

steps.title: רב יוסף explains רבי אליעזר: no טובת הנאה, so benefit is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר does not require naming the tithe. So he holds a doubt does not make the produce טבל, there is no טובת הנאה, and the woman may benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says you do not designate it by name holds that the doubt does not make it טבל. Whenever the doubt does not make it טבל, the owner has no right to choose who gets it, so she is allowed to benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף finishes his proof by explaining the other side, רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב יוסף's reading, the whole מחלוקת depends on one linked question: does the doubt make it טבל, and does the owner have טובת הנאה? For רבי אליעזר the answer to both is no, so the woman who vowed may take the tithe.

keyTerms.meaning: The doubt does not make it forbidden as טבל.
Permitted.
To benefit.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says he does not designate it by name,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording, and it makes this line about רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: he holds: its doubt does not make it טבל,
and whenever its doubt does not make it טבל
the owner does not have the benefit of discretion,
and she is permitted to benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof by explaining the opposing view.
steps.raayaObject: That the dispute over טבל is tied to the dispute over טובת הנאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's view that the מעשר עני of דמאי does not need to be named.

steps.title: אביי: everyone agrees the doubt makes it טבל
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. Both sides agree that a doubt makes the produce טבל, and they argue about something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: everyone agrees the doubt makes it טבל. רבי אליעזר and חכמים argue about this:
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף. He sets up a different explanation of the argument, which he gives in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both sides agree about טבל, the מחלוקת says nothing about טובת הנאה, and רב יוסף's proof falls apart. אביי still has to explain what they do argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees.
They argue about this, introducing the real point of the argument.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Everyone agrees its doubt makes it טבל,
and Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis disagree about this:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא סְפֵקוֹ טוֹבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's reading of the מחלוקת.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the מחלוקת to טובת הנאה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes they argue about whether the doubt makes it טבל. They may instead argue about something unrelated to טובת הנאה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: עמי הארץ are not suspected about מעשר עני
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, רבי אליעזר trusts עמי הארץ to separate מעשר עני. The reason is that an עם הארץ could make himself poor and keep the tithe, so separating it costs him nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds: עמי הארץ are not suspected of skipping the poor man's tithe. If he declared his property ownerless, he would become poor and could take the tithe himself, so he has no loss.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains רבי אליעזר's real reason for not requiring the tithe to be named.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People skip tithes when tithing costs them money. Here, the עם הארץ could declare his property ownerless and take the מעשר עני himself, so he loses nothing. That is why רבי אליעזר assumes he separated it, and the buyer of דמאי does not need to name it.

keyTerms.meaning: They are suspected.
Unlearned people who are not careful about tithes.
Declares his property ownerless (הפקר).
A loss.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְשְׁדוּ עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ עַל מַעְשַׂר עָנִי.
phrases.english: עמי הארץ are not suspected regarding the poor man's tithe.
Since if he were to declare his property ownerless
and become poor and take it himself,
he has no loss.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: לֹא נֶחְשְׁדוּ עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ עַל מַעְשַׂר עָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in רבי אליעזר's side of אביי's new explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Gives another reason for רבי אליעזר's ruling, one that has nothing to do with טובת הנאה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר's view can be explained by trust in עמי הארץ, not by a view about טבל.

steps.title: חכמים: people do not give up their property, so עמי הארץ are suspected
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, חכמים say no one actually makes his property ownerless, because someone else might grab it. So separating the tithe really costs the עם הארץ money, and he is suspected of skipping it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים hold: a person does not declare his property ownerless, because he is afraid someone else might acquire it. Therefore they are suspected.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his explanation with the view of חכמים. This completes the rejection of רב יוסף's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making yourself poor is possible in theory, but no one actually risks losing everything to keep a tithe. So tithing is a real loss for the עם הארץ, and חכמים suspect he skipped it. The argument is about trusting עמי הארץ, not about טובת הנאה, so רב יוסף's proof fails. The next step gives רבא's different answer about the woman's case.

keyTerms.meaning: He is afraid.
Acquires.
Therefore.

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף tied the מחלוקת to טבל and טובת הנאה. אביי showed it could instead be about whether עמי הארץ are trusted with מעשר עני. So the proof about the woman's vow does not work.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
A person does not declare his property ownerless,
because he is afraid that perhaps
another person will acquire them.
Therefore, they are suspected.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the עמי הארץ. The suspicion is about skipping מעשר עני.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: נִכְסֵיהּ לָא מַפְקַר אִינִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of אביי's explanation, completing the rejection.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Finishes showing that the מחלוקת has nothing to do with טובת הנאה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חכמים's ruling comes from suspecting עמי הארץ, not from a position on טובת הנאה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof from דמאי fails. רבא answers the question of the woman taking מעשר עני differently in Steps 7-8.

steps.title: רבא: Tithe given out in the house counts as benefit
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the source forbidding the woman to take מעשר עני is talking about tithe handed out at home, where the Torah says 'give,' so the owner chooses the recipient.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: Here the source is talking about poor man's tithe that is handed out inside the house. The Torah uses the word 'give' about it: 'And you shall give to the לוי, to the stranger...' Because of that, she is forbidden to benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts his own way of settling the sources, so they no longer have to depend on a מחלוקת. This first half covers tithe that is handed out at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When מעשר עני is brought home, the owner hands it out himself and chooses which poor person gets it. The פסוק says 'וְנָתַתָּ' (you shall give), so the owner holds טובת הנאה. Taking from him therefore means getting a benefit from a person, and the woman who vowed off benefit from people may not take it.

keyTerms.meaning: Poor man's tithe, given to the poor in the 3rd and 6th years of the שמיטה cycle
Handed out inside the house, after the produce was brought home
Giving; this word shows the owner actively hands it to someone he picks
To benefit

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the woman is forbidden to take all מעשר עני. It depends on how the tithe is handed out. This step covers only the at-home case.

phrases.english: Rava says:
Here, it is talking about poor man's tithe
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the source that forbids the woman to take the tithe.

phrases.english: that is handed out inside the house,
since 'giving' is written about it:
"And you shall give to the Levite, to the stranger, etc."
Because of that, it is forbidden for her to benefit from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אוֹמֵר: כָּאן בְּמַעְשַׂר עָנִי הַמִּתְחַלֵּק בְּתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי's explanation, רבא offers a different way to settle the sources: two different cases instead of a מחלוקת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the sources talk about two different ways of handing out the tithe.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources contradict each other, so they must reflect a מחלוקת תנאים about whether a doubt makes the produce טבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tithe handed out at home carries טובת הנאה, so she may not take it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the need to tie the sources to a מחלוקת about doubtful טבל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The difference comes from how the tithe is handed out, not from any disagreement about the law.

steps.title: רבא: Tithe left at the threshing floor is not benefit
steps.stepSummary: The other source, which lets her take the tithe, is talking about tithe left at the threshing floors, where the Torah says 'leave it,' so the owner does not choose who takes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the source is talking about poor man's tithe handed out at the threshing floors. Since the Torah writes about it 'and you shall leave it in your gates,' she is allowed to benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of רבא's answer. It explains the source that lets her take the tithe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the threshing floor the owner just 'leaves' the tithe out (וְהִנַּחְתָּ), and any poor person who comes may take it. The owner has no say over who gets it, so there is no טובת הנאה. She is not getting anything from a person, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing floors, where the grain is processed in the field
'And you shall leave it in your gates', so the tithe is left out for anyone to take
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: in the house the Torah says 'give,' so the owner chooses and taking is forbidden. At the threshing floor the Torah says 'leave,' so anyone takes and taking is permitted.

phrases.english: There, it is talking about poor man's tithe
phrases.notes: Here 'כאן' points to the other source, the one that lets her take the tithe.

phrases.english: that is handed out at the threshing floors.
Since it is written about it:
"And you shall leave it within your gates,"
she is permitted to benefit from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן בְּמַעְשַׂר עָנִי הַמִּתְחַלֵּק בְּתוֹךְ הַגֳּרָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's split by giving the second case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tithe left at the threshing floor carries no טובת הנאה, so she may take it.

steps.title: The משנה implies the right to choose is not money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if someone forbids כהנים and לוים to benefit from him, they may still take their gifts. This suggests טובת הנאה is not worth money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if someone says 'כהנים and לוים may not benefit from me,' they may take their gifts anyway. Apparently, the right to choose who gets the gifts is not money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה and draws an inference from it about טובת הנאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner's right to choose which כהן gets his gifts were worth money, then forbidding כהנים to benefit from him would stop them from taking. Since the משנה lets them take anyway, the owner's right to choose seems to have no money value.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהנים and לוים, who receive תרומה and מעשר
Benefit from me; in a נדר it means 'are forbidden to benefit from me'
They may take, even against the owner's will
Apparently / this shows that
Is not money; has no value you can own

phrases.english: "Priests and Levites shall not benefit from me"
they may take, etc.
Apparently, the benefit of choosing the recipient is not worth money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next line of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That טובת הנאה is not considered money
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first part of the משנה: the כהנים and לוים may take the gifts despite the נדר

steps.title: The end of the משנה implies the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The end of the same משנה says that if he named specific כהנים and לוים, only others may take, and those specific ones may not. This suggests טובת הנאה is worth money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now look at the end of the משנה: if he said 'these כהנים and these לוים may not benefit from me,' others take the gifts, but these ones may not. Apparently, the right to choose is worth money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference it just made, using the end of the same משנה. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner can block specific כהנים from getting his gifts, his choice must mean something. That makes his right to choose a real value he can forbid. So the first part of the משנה suggests טובת הנאה is not money, and the end suggests it is money. The two parts seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the end part (of the משנה), used to bring a contradiction
These specific ones
Others

steps.confusionAlert: Both inferences come from the same משנה. The difference is whether he forbade כהנים and לוים in general or named specific ones.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
"These priests and these Levites shall not benefit from me"
others take the gifts,
but these ones may not.
Apparently, the benefit of choosing is worth money!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: כֹּהֲנִים אֵלּוּ וּלְוִיִּם אֵלּוּ נֶהֱנִין לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the inference from the first part of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that טובת הנאה is not money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the משנה lets the owner block specific כהנים. That only makes sense if his right to choose is worth money, so the two parts of the משנה contradict each other.

steps.title: רב הושעיא: the two halves follow two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא says there is no contradiction. The end of the משנה follows רבי, and the beginning follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: It is not difficult. This part follows רבי, and that part follows רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא answers the contradiction from Step 10. He says the two halves of the משנה come from two different תנאים who disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not force one view to explain both halves of the משנה. Instead it splits them. The end, where specific כהנים are barred and so טובת הנאה counts as money, follows רבי. The beginning, where it does not count as money, follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one... and that one... (a way to assign each source to a different case or opinion)
רבי יהודה הנשיא, who arranged the משנה
A תנא, the son of רבי יהודה

steps.confusionAlert: "This" and "that" do not follow the order of the משנה. The first one named, רבי, matches the END of the משנה, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה matches the BEGINNING.

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said: It is not difficult;

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי, וְהָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: this is Rabbi, and that is Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the end of the משנה, about specific כהנים, which follows רבי; 'that' is the beginning, which follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי, וְהָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 10 between the two halves of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the source between two תנאים who disagree (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One משנה should follow one view, so its two halves seem to contradict each other about טובת הנאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two halves follow two different תנאים. רבי holds that טובת הנאה is worth money, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that it is not.

steps.title: A ברייתא: how much does a thief pay for stolen טבל?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records an argument. רבי says a thief who ate someone's טבל pays its full value. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says he pays only for the חולין part.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: One who steals his friend's untithed produce and eats it pays him the value of his untithed produce. These are the words of רבי. רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה says: He pays only the value of the non-sacred part in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה really do argue about something like this. The case is a thief who steals and eats טבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבל still contains the תרומה and מעשר, which belong to the כהן and לוי, not to the owner. רבי makes the thief pay for everything. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה makes him pay only for the חולין, the part that truly belongs to the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Produce from which תרומה and מעשר have not yet been separated
One who steals
Ordinary, non-holy produce; here, the part of the טבל that is not תרומה or מעשר

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: הַגּוֹנֵב טִבְלוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ וַאֲכָלוֹ —
phrases.english: As it is taught: One who steals his friend's untithed produce and eats it

phrases.aramaic: מְשַׁלֵּם לוֹ דְּמֵי טִבְלוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי.
phrases.english: pays him the value of his untithed produce; these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם אֶלָּא דְּמֵי חוּלִּין שֶׁבּוֹ.
phrases.english: He pays only the value of the non-sacred part in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הַגּוֹנֵב טִבְלוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ וַאֲכָלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source showing that the two תנאים named by רב הושעיא argue about a related case.
steps.raayaObject: רב הושעיא's claim that רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagree about whether טובת הנאה is worth money.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a thief who eats stolen טבל: רבי says he pays full value, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says he pays only for the חולין.

steps.title: Is their argument about טובת הנאה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to suggest that רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argue about exactly this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they disagree about this:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts to suggest what the ברייתא's argument is really about, and the full suggestion comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "מאי לאו" offers a reading that would tie the ברייתא to רב הושעיא's answer. The idea being built is that the argument over the thief's payment depends on whether the owner's טובת הנאה in the gifts is worth money. The rest of the suggestion continues in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that...? (introduces a suggested reading)
They disagree

phrases.english: What, is it not that they disagree about this:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to explain how the ברייתא's argument connects to the question of טובת הנאה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the argument between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה about the thief's payment is really an argument about whether טובת הנאה is worth money.
